correctness.rationale: For distinct vertices only their head-to-head Bernoulli result is shared; remaining wins are independent Bin(n-2,1/2). The cross-covariance equals minus one-quarter the product of binomial finite differences. Binomial summation by parts equates each finite difference with 4/(n-1) times covariance with B. Summing same- and cross-vertex terms yields the universal bilinear identity. Basis functions yield a rank-two correction, whose vectors have exact norm one and zero inner product. The projector, rank, spectrum, and Pearson trace then hold for all n≥2, including n=2. Independent exact enumeration of 33,866 labeled tournaments through n=6 checks every one of 90 covariance entries and five Pearson expectations.

value.rationale: The binomial-weighted full score-frequency spectrum determines covariances of all empirical score functionals at once and proves that only total count and total wins exhaust exact linear constraints. The exact expected Pearson discrepancy equals n-2, calibrating a canonical full-histogram statistic whose vertex observations are dependent, whereas multinomial calibration would give n-1. This motivated structural identity is not an arbitrary selected finite slice, a normalization artifact, or a textbook moment of one vertex.
